C4.rationale: Level 2 (demoted from 3 on evidence review): DRAM90013 (Independent Dramaturgy Project, 37.5 points, the program's largest single subject) is presented as the culmination/synthesis subject in which each student independently identifies and establishes the parameters of their own project, and DRAM90018 documents structured progression toward it. All three evidenceLines are Overview/Intended-learning-outcomes text, not text drawn from DRAM90013's actual Assessment page; R2 holds that an outcome statement alone is never sufficient for Level 3. No assessment-task text was quoted to substantiate the capstone claim at demotion time, even though such text exists unquoted elsewhere in the source (extract lines 689/694/699) — a fresh capture and scoring pass against that assessment-page text could support Level 3, but this pass does not raise the score without it.

C5.rationale: Level 2: DRAM90010 (Performing Arts Research Methodologies) trains methodology selection, assessed via 'Identifying research questions and methodologies appropriate to own practice' (40%). DRAM90013's required Independent Dramaturgy Project generates primary practice-based evidence via a substantial required project, documented ('journal and formal documentation of research materials; observation of rehearsals/meetings') and critically analysed in a synthesising essay — methodology selection and primary evidence generation, assessed. Level 3 additionally requires methodology defended under scrutiny (viva, defence, or staged supervised review). DRAM90013 includes a '30-minute oral presentation on project' (20%), which plausibly serves this function, but unlike THTR90009's presentation (explicitly '(plus Q&A)'), the extract does not state that DRAM90013's presentation involves examiner challenge or defence of methodology. Ambiguous between Level 2 and 3; resolved to the lower Level 2.

W1.rationale: Level 2: recognised professional genres recur across core units — an 'Industry Pitch Document' (DRAM90019, 30%), a '15-minute Project pitch presentation' (DRAM90018, 30%), and 'Critical evaluation of a dramaturgical feedback session with a writer' (DRAM90024, 30%) — reinforced by outcomes such as DRAM90023's 'comport a professional demeanour in a leadership role appropriate to the working context'. Level 3 additionally requires at least one core assessment delivered to, or judged by, a real external audience or practitioner, with professional conduct/accountability explicitly assessed. DRAM90011 places students as a working dramaturg in an actual VCA production, and DRAM90013 places them on productions 'in the main stage or independent theatre arena locally, nationally or internationally' — real external contexts — but the extract documents these assessments (journals, essays, presentations) as judged by the unit coordinator, not by an external practitioner or industry panel. Ambiguous between Level 2 and 3; resolved to the lower Level 2.

W3.rationale: Level 2: DRAM90013 (Independent Dramaturgy Project, required, 37.5 points) places each student as a dramaturg or assistant dramaturg on a real production 'happening at the Victorian College of the Arts (VCA) or in the main stage or independent theatre arena locally, nationally or internationally', assessed via engagement evidenced by journal, documentation and observation, plus a synthesising critical-analysis essay — a core unit placing students in a real production setting with assessment. Level 3 requires an extended placement or a sequence of them, supervised by a practitioner, with accountability to the host and structured reflection. DRAM90013 is a single (if large) required subject rather than a documented sequence, and the extract never states that a practitioner (as distinct from the university unit coordinator) supervises the placement, nor that students are accountable to the host. DRAM90018's outcome references 'their internship semester 1', but no internship subject page or assessment appears in the extract to substantiate it. Ambiguous between Level 2 and 3; resolved to the lower Level 2 given the missing supervision/accountability evidence.

G1.rationale: The course structure is explicitly '150-point program of compulsory subjects' — every listed subject across both years is compulsory, with a staged/progressive sequence (DRAM90011 Applied Dramaturgy 1 -> DRAM90023 Applied Dramaturgy 2, explicitly 'Drawing on the learning from Applied Dramaturgy 1' -> DRAM90013 Independent Dramaturgy Project capstone) within a named specialist discipline ('the first and only course leading to a qualification in dramaturgy in Australia and Asia'). This is an all-compulsory specialist core with progressive depth.
